title: Oriented Reidemeister moves
statement: An **oriented Reidemeister move** is one of the following local replacements, performed inside a small disk while the diagram is unchanged outside it and up to planar isotopy outside the disk, with all sign and orientation variants included: (R1) create or delete a kink on one strand, the two signs of the kink both allowed; (R2) slide one strand over or under a neighbouring strand so as to create or delete two crossings of opposite signs; (R3) move one strand across an existing crossing of two other strands, replacing the three-crossing local picture by the picture with the crossing moved to the other side. The strands keep their orientations throughout, so the move list contains every orientation pattern occurring in the three figures.
strategy: The complete (all signs and orientations) list is needed because the oriented Markov and Alexander constructions below act on oriented diagrams; the local models are those of the sources' figures.

references.title: Ozsvath, Stipsicz and Szabo, Grid Homology for Knots and Links, AMS Surveys and Monographs 208 (2015); section 2.1 and Appendix B.1, printed pp. 367-372
Queffelec, Reidemeister's theorem using transversality, Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society (2024); arXiv:2406.18203v1, sections 2-3
Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
